title: IOL Power Calculation After Refractive Surgery
summary: Navigating the 'Double Error' of keratometry and ELP prediction to achieve emmetropia in the post-LASIK, PRK, and RK era. A comprehensive guide for high-precision surgical planning.

sections.title: The Fundamental Challenge: The 'Double Error'
sections.content: Standard IOL calculation formulas fail post-refractive surgery due to two primary errors: 1. Keratometric Error (Incorrectly assuming the ratio of anterior-to-posterior corneal curvature is 1.21 after the anterior surface is altered) and 2. ELP Error (Standard formulas use K-values to predict the Effective Lens Position; flattened corneas lead the formula to predict a more shallow ACD, resulting in an underpowered IOL and a hyperopic surprise).

rows: Standard keratometers measure 3.2mm zone, missing the central effective power.
Keratometers use n=1.3375 based on virgin corneas; surgery changes the n-ratio.
Formula assumes flat cornea = shallow AC; erroneously places IOL too far anterior.

sections.title: Pre-Operative Diagnostic Workup
content: Obtain prior surgical records (Pre-op K, Manifest Refraction, Surgically Induced Refractive Change).
Perform Scheimpflug Tomography (Pentacam) or OCT-based Pachymetry.
Measure 'True Net Power' or 'Total Corneal Refractive Power' (TCRP).
Axial Length (AL) measurement via Optical Biometry (Lenstar/IOLMaster 700).
Assess for corneal ectasia or irregular astigmatism.
Dry eye management (aggressive treatment before measurements).

branches: Methods based on Clinical History (e.g., Clinical History Method)
Methods based on Adjusted K (e.g., Masket, Modified Masket)
Methods based on No Prior Data (e.g., Barrett True-K, Haigis-L, Shammas)
Direct Measurement (e.g., OCT-based, Ray Tracing, Pentacam TNP)

sections.title: The Gold Standard: Barrett True-K
sections.content: The Barrett True-K formula is a universal formula that accommodates both myopic and hyperopic LASIK/PRK, as well as Radial Keratotomy (RK). It uses a modified Universal II formula and incorporates a predicted posterior corneal curvature and a proprietary ELP adjustment to correct the double-error phenomenon. It is currently the most validated method in literature.

sections.title: Red Flags: Critical Errors to Avoid
content: NEVER use standard formulas (SRK/T, Hoffer Q, Holladay 1) without specific adjustments.
Do not rely on a single calculation method; use the ASCRS online calculator for consensus.
Avoid multifocal IOLs in patients with significant corneal higher-order aberrations (>0.4 μm).
Watch for RK patients with fluctuating vision (diurnal variation).

sections.title: Radial Keratotomy (RK) Considerations
content: RK corneas are extremely unstable and often hyperfocal centrally.
Target a myopic outcome (-0.75D to -1.25D) to account for potential hyperopic shifts.
Calculate using the Barrett True-K (RK) or the Double-K modified formulas.
Avoid large incisions that intersect RK scars.
Incisions should be placed between RK scars to prevent 'fish-mouthing'.

content.explanation: Flat corneas Lead to Anterior Targeting (formula thinks IOL is too far forward), resulting in Low-power IOL selection and a Troublesome hyperopic surprise.

sections.title: Management Workflow (The ASCRS Algorithm)
content: Step 1: Determine the type of prior surgery (Myopic LASIK, Hyperopic LASIK, or RK).
Step 2: Collect data (Historical records, Biometry, Tomography).
Step 3: Enter data into the ASCRS Online Post-Refractive Calculator.
Step 4: Compare results from Barrett True-K, Haigis-L, and Shammas-PL.
Step 5: Select the IOL power based on the 'Average' or 'Min' value depending on surgeon preference.
Step 6: Adjust target to -0.50D for LASIK/PRK and -1.00D for RK.

sections.title: IOL Selection Pearls
content: Use aspheric Monofocal IOLs with negative spherical aberration (e.g., Tecnis, AcrySof IQ) to counteract positive corneal aberration in post-myopic LASIK.
Use neutral aspheric IOLs (e.g., enVista, SofPort LI61AO) for post-hyperopic LASIK.
Small-aperture IOLs (IC-8) are excellent for irregular corneas/RK.
Toric IOLs should be used with extreme caution (ensure axis stability and regularity).

sections.title: Intraoperative Aberrometry (ORA)
sections.content: Intraoperative wavefront aberrometry (e.g., Alcon ORA) provides real-time refractive data after the cataract is removed (aphakic state). It is a powerful adjunct that bypasses corneal measurement errors by measuring the whole eye's refractive power, though it can be influenced by speculum pressure and corneal hydration.

content.explanation: Calculates central power from topography: (Central Power x 1.114) - 6.1. Useful when no prior history is available but topography is accessible.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for the Fellow
content: Always warn the patient about the high possibility of a 'refractive surprise' and potential for IOL exchange.
Check the 'Corneal Sphericity' — if highly irregular, avoid complex optics.
If using ORA, ensure the eye is at physiologic IOP before the measurement.
The 'Clinical History Method' is now considered less reliable than modern formula-based approaches.
